summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever, cough, dysuria, and worsening back pain, five days after discharge for a UTI. She was found to have multifocal pneumonia on chest imaging, a supratherapeutic INR of 14, and a coagulase-negative staphylococcus in urine likely representing contamination. She was treated with a seven-day course of IV cefepime and linezolid for pneumonia, which resolved her fever and respiratory symptoms. Her INR was corrected with vitamin K and temporary warfarin hold, then restarted at 10 mg daily with normalization. A rash that developed on admission was attributed to vancomycin allergy and resolved with discontinuation and antihistamines. Bactrim was stopped after three days as the urine culture was deemed non-significant. She remained afebrile, asymptomatic, and stable, with improvement in labs and respiratory status, and was discharged home on her prior medications with follow-up for INR monitoring and psychosocial support.
